mandatory_modal_verb.note: The only acceptable modal for binding requirements per ARP4754A and DO-178C writing conventions.

ears_patterns.description: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) patterns for rewriting requirements. The recommender agent SHALL choose the most appropriate pattern based on the requirement nature.
ears_patterns.reference: Mavin et al., EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), IEEE RE 2009.

patterns.name: Ubiquitous
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies always, unconditionally, with no trigger or precondition.
patterns.example: The Flight Control System shall respond to pilot inputs within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Event-Driven
patterns.template: WHEN <trigger> [<optional precondition>], the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement is triggered by a discrete event or stimulus.
patterns.example: WHEN the pilot applies a control input, the Flight Control System shall generate a surface deflection command within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Unwanted Behavior
patterns.template: IF <unwanted condition or event>, THEN the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement specifies the system response to a fault, failure, or off-nominal condition.
patterns.example: IF a sensor failure is detected, THEN the Flight Control System shall switch to the redundant sensor within 50 ms.

patterns.name: State-Driven
patterns.template: WHILE <system state>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies continuously during a specific operating state or mode.
patterns.example: WHILE in degraded mode, the Flight Control System shall maintain attitude control with an accuracy of ±2°.

patterns.name: Optional Feature
patterns.template: WHERE <feature is included>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies only when an optional feature or configuration is present.
patterns.example: WHERE the enhanced autopilot feature is installed, the Flight Control System shall provide envelope protection.

patterns.name: Complex
patterns.template: (Combination of two or more EARS patterns above.)
patterns.use_when: The requirement involves multiple triggers, states, or conditions that cannot be cleanly separated without losing meaning.
patterns.example: WHILE in cruise mode, WHEN the autopilot is engaged, the Flight Control System shall maintain altitude within ±50 ft.

rules.title: Unique requirement identifier
rules.objective: Ensure each requirement is uniquely identifiable
checks: [RULE-C01.a] Verify the requirement has an identifier
[RULE-C01.b] Verify the identifier adheres to the project naming convention

rules.title: Operational modes specified
rules.objective: Ensure applicability conditions are stated
checks: [RULE-C03.a] Verify operational modes or conditions are explicitly stated
[RULE-C03.b] Verify missing or implicit operational assumptions
[RULE-C03.c] Verify behavior during mode transitions is explicitly defined

rules.title: Acceptance criteria defined
rules.objective: Ensure requirement can be accepted objectively
checks: [RULE-C04.a] Detect measurable criteria or referenced verification method
[RULE-C04.b] Verify requirements without acceptance criteria

rules.title: Safety requirements reference DAL
rules.objective: Ensure safety requirements reference failure conditions and DAL
checks: [RULE-C05.a] Identify safety-related requirements
[RULE-C05.b] Verify associated failure condition and DAL are specified

rules.title: Requirement source identified
rules.objective: Ensure traceability to origin
checks: [RULE-C06.a] Verify presence of source or rationale
[RULE-C06.b] Classify source as regulatory, customer, or derived

rules.title: Derived requirements justified
rules.objective: Ensure derived requirements are documented and safety-routed
checks: [RULE-C07.a] Identify derived requirements
[RULE-C07.b] Verify justification or derivation rationale exists
[RULE-C07.c] Verify derived requirements are routed to the safety process (FHA/PSSA)

rules.title: Coverage of system functions
rules.objective: Ensure all FHA functions are covered by requirements
checks: [RULE-C08.a] Compare requirement coverage against FHA functions
[RULE-C08.b] Identify missing functional coverage

rules.title: Interface requirements completeness
rules.objective: Ensure interfaces are fully specified
checks: [RULE-C09.a] Verify protocols, data formats, and timing are defined
[RULE-C09.b] Verify partially specified interfaces
[RULE-C09.c] Verify system response to invalid inputs, out-of-range data, or missing signals is defined

rules.title: Environmental requirements specified
rules.objective: Ensure environmental constraints are stated where applicable
checks: [RULE-C10.a] Detect environmental constraints applicability
[RULE-C10.b] Verify explicit limits are defined

rules.title: No contradictory requirements
rules.objective: Eliminate logical contradictions across the requirement set
checks: [RULE-K01.a] Perform pairwise semantic contradiction analysis
[RULE-K01.b] Verify conflicting constraints or behaviors
[RULE-K01.c] Verify semantic equivalence (duplicate requirements)
[RULE-K01.d] Verify subsuming requirements (one requirement fully contained in another)

rules.title: Consistent terminology
rules.objective: Ensure uniform use of terms across the requirement set
checks: [RULE-K02.a] Extract key terms from all requirements
[RULE-K02.b] Detect inconsistent usage or definitions of the same term
[RULE-K02.c] Verify terms against the approved project Data Dictionary or Glossary

rules.title: Consistent units and tolerances
rules.objective: Prevent unit or tolerance mismatches across requirements
checks: [RULE-K03.a] Detect physical quantities and their units in all requirements
[RULE-K03.b] Verify unit and tolerance consistency across the requirement set

rules.title: Consistent DAL allocation
rules.objective: Ensure DAL assignments are consistent with safety assessments
checks: [RULE-K04.a] Compare DAL assignments with FHA/PSSA
[RULE-K04.b] Verify any mismatch between assigned DAL and failure condition severity

rules.title: Performance feasibility
rules.objective: Ensure performance requirements are consistent with known HW/SW constraints
checks: [RULE-K05.a] Compare performance requirements with HW/SW constraints
[RULE-K05.b] Verify infeasible or contradictory performance requirements

rules.title: Timing consistency
rules.objective: Ensure timing constraints do not conflict across requirements
checks: [RULE-K06.a] Extract all timing constraints from the requirement set
[RULE-K06.b] Detect conflicting latency, period, or deadline requirements

rules.title: Requirement is verifiable
rules.objective: Ensure objective verification is possible
checks: [RULE-V01.a] Verify a verification approach exists for the requirement
[RULE-V01.b] Reject unverifiable statements that cannot be tested, analysed, inspected, or demonstrated

rules.title: Quantified performance thresholds
rules.objective: Ensure performance criteria are measurable
checks: [RULE-V02.a] Detect numeric thresholds and tolerances in the requirement
[RULE-V02.b] Verify vague performance statements that lack numeric criteria (value + unit + tolerance)

rules.title: No subjective terms without measurable backing
rules.objective: Eliminate purely subjective requirements
checks: [RULE-V03.a] Detect subjective or qualitative wording
[RULE-V03.b] Verify measurable acceptance criteria exist for every subjective term

rules.title: Verification method mapped
rules.objective: Ensure a verification method is identified for the requirement
checks: [RULE-V04.a] Verify mapping to at least one of Test (T), Analysis (A), Inspection (I), Demonstration (D)
[RULE-V04.b] Verify the specific phase or level of verification is identified

rules.title: Verification feasibility
rules.objective: Ensure verification can realistically be performed
checks: [RULE-V05.a] Assess feasibility of the required verification against project test capabilities and constraints

rules.title: No impossible verification conditions
rules.objective: Avoid undefined or impossible states in the requirement
checks: [RULE-V06.a] Detect physically impossible states or undefined references in the requirement text

rules.title: Traceability to higher-level requirements
rules.objective: Ensure upward traceability to parent or regulatory source
checks: [RULE-T01.a] Verify link to aircraft-level, regulatory, or customer requirement
[RULE-T01.b] Identify orphaned requirements that have no parent trace

rules.title: Derived requirement traceability
rules.objective: Ensure derived requirements are traceable to their justification
checks: [RULE-T02.a] Verify link to safety assessment (FHA/PSSA/SSA) or documented design decision

rules.title: Downward traceability
rules.objective: Ensure every requirement links to implementation artifacts
checks: [RULE-T03.a] Verify trace to design or code elements exists
[RULE-T03.b] Verify 100% downward coverage (no requirement lacks downstream allocation)

rules.title: HW/SW allocation documented
rules.objective: Ensure hardware/software allocation is specified for each requirement
checks: [RULE-T04.a] Verify HW/SW allocation documentation exists for the requirement

rules.title: FHA failure condition traceability
rules.objective: Ensure each FHA failure condition maps to at least one safety requirement
checks: [RULE-T05.a] Verify each FHA failure condition is covered by at least one safety requirement

rules.title: Correct system behavior
rules.objective: Ensure the requirement reflects the intended system behavior
checks: [RULE-R01.a] Compare requirement intent with the system definition
[RULE-R01.b] Verify adherence to known physical or mathematical boundaries

rules.title: No unnecessary design constraints
rules.objective: Avoid premature design decisions in requirements
checks: [RULE-R02.a] Detect implementation-specific wording
[RULE-R02.b] Verify the requirement states what the system must do, not how it should be implemented

rules.title: Single obligation per statement
rules.objective: Avoid compound requirements — one 'shall' per statement
checks: [RULE-R04.a] Count the number of 'shall' occurrences
[RULE-R04.b] Detect multiple obligations joined by 'and' or 'or' within a single statement
[RULE-R04.c] Split compound requirements into separate requirements

rules.title: Appropriate abstraction level
rules.objective: Ensure the requirement is written at the correct hierarchy level
checks: [RULE-R05.a] Assess abstraction level relative to the requirement hierarchy (aircraft, system, item)

rules.title: Explicit assumptions
rules.objective: Ensure all assumptions underlying the requirement are documented
checks: [RULE-R06.a] Detect implicit assumptions embedded in the requirement text
[RULE-R06.b] Verify every assumption is explicitly stated

rulesets.description: Lexical wording rules — markers that unconditionally invalidate a requirement

rules.title: Unambiguous requirement wording
rules.objective: Eliminate ambiguity — every term must be defined or measurable
checks: [RULE-C02.a] Detect vague performance terms such as fast, slow, quickly, soon, rapidly, timely
[RULE-C02.b] Detect vague quantitative terms such as approximately, about, around, roughly
[RULE-C02.c] Detect vague quantification terms such as adequate, sufficient, appropriate, suitable, negligible
[RULE-C02.d] Detect vague conditional applicability terms such as as required, if applicable, where necessary, when needed
[RULE-C02.e] Detect subjective quality judgment terms such as good, bad, better, best, optimal, acceptable, reasonable
[RULE-C02.f] Detect vague performance attribute terms such as reliable, robust, flexible, efficient
[RULE-C02.g] Detect vague usability attribute terms such as user-friendly, intuitive, easy, simple
[RULE-C02.h] Detect vague optimization terms such as minimize, maximize
[RULE-C02.i] Detect vague state classification terms such as normal, abnormal
[RULE-C02.j] Detect vague scale reference terms such as high, low, large, small
[RULE-C02.k] Detect reference to implementation solution

rules.title: Correct modal verb — 'shall' mandatory
rules.objective: Ensure 'shall' is the sole modal for all binding obligations
checks: [RULE-R03.a] Verify 'shall' is used for every binding obligation
[RULE-R03.b] Detect weak or non-standard modals that may appear in binding obligations
[RULE-R03.d] Detect capability modal 'can'
[RULE-R03.e] Detect non-standard modal 'must'
[RULE-R03.f] Detect intent modal 'will'
[RULE-R03.g] Detect passive paraphrase 'is required to'
[RULE-R03.h] Detect weak phrase 'should be able to'

rules.title: No TBD placeholders
rules.objective: Ensure all values are defined before review
checks: [RULE-W01.a] Detect the literal string 'TBD' (case-sensitive) anywhere in the requirement text
[RULE-W01.b] Reject requirements containing 'TBD'

rules.title: No TBC placeholders
rules.objective: Ensure all values are confirmed before review
checks: [RULE-W02.a] Detect the literal string 'TBC' (case-sensitive) anywhere in the requirement text
[RULE-W02.b] Reject requirements containing 'TBC'

rulesets.origin: ARP4754A writing conventions + project wording guide
rulesets.description: Sentence structure and morphology rules — clarity, active voice, unambiguous reference

rules.title: No negation issues
rules.objective: Express obligations as positive, measurable statements
checks: [RULE-M01.a] [double_negation] Detect two negation markers in the same clause
[RULE-M01.b] [hidden_negation] Detect implicit negative constructions
[RULE-M01.c] [negative_requirement] Detect requirements expressed in negative form

rules.title: No structural complexity
rules.objective: Keep each requirement simple, focused, and parseable
checks: [RULE-M02.a] [long_sentences] Verify sentences exceeding 30 words
[RULE-M02.b] [multiple_subordinate_clauses] Detect stacked dependent clauses
[RULE-M02.c] [nested_conditions] Detect multiple embedded IF/WHEN/WHILE structures

rules.title: Unambiguous references and explicit subject
rules.objective: Every pronoun and reference must have a clear, named antecedent
checks: [RULE-M03.a] [ambiguous_pronouns] Detect 'it', 'this', 'that', 'they', 'them' without a clear antecedent
[RULE-M03.b] [unclear_references] Detect 'the system' when multiple systems are in scope
[RULE-M03.c] [dangling_modifiers] Detect modifiers not clearly attached to the subject they qualify
[RULE-M03.d] [implicit_subject] Verify the grammatical subject of 'shall' is an identifiable system or function

rules.title: Active voice
rules.objective: Use active voice to make the obligated entity explicit
checks: [RULE-M04.a] Detect agentless passive constructions
[RULE-M04.b] Rewrite passive constructions into active voice

rules.title: No mixed modality
rules.objective: Use a single, consistent modal within each requirement statement
checks: [RULE-M05.a] Detect the combination of 'shall' with 'should', 'may', or 'can' within the same requirement statement
[RULE-M05.b] Resolve to a single modal (use 'shall' if the obligation is binding)

rules.title: No logical ambiguity
rules.objective: Make logical structure and conjunctions explicit and unambiguous
checks: [RULE-M06.a] [and_or_combination] Detect 'and/or'
[RULE-M06.b] [implicit_conditions] Detect conditions not explicitly introduced by IF, WHEN, WHILE, or WHERE
[RULE-M06.c] [temporal_ambiguity] Detect unclear sequences of events

rules.title: No vagueness in structure
rules.objective: Ensure requirements are complete, closed, and self-standing
checks: [RULE-M07.a] [open_ended_lists] Detect 'etc.', 'etc', 'and/or', 'including but not limited to'
[RULE-M07.b] [incomplete_sentences] Detect sentence fragments

rules.title: Sentence length
rules.objective: Keep sentences concise for clarity and parsability
checks: [RULE-M08.a] Count words in the requirement statement
[RULE-M08.b] Verify word count exceeds 30
